meta.scope: Yangon-centred history of Myanmar / Burmese hip-hop: artists, crews, releases, songs, events, venues, topics, sources and typed relationships.

provenance.model: Every claim carries at least one source id. `status` on relationships is one of VERIFIED (human-checked), AI_EXTRACTED (pending review), CONFLICTED, REJECTED. `confidence` is high | medium | low.
provenance.copyright: Factual metadata only (names, dates, places). No article text, lyrics or images are redistributed. Copyrighted sources are cited for facts only.
provenance.caveat: Entities marked confidence low or status AI_EXTRACTED have not been human-verified. Render these with a visible "unverified" affordance.

guide.purpose: Single-file JSON for LLM consumption and UI generation. All cross-references are already resolved: nothing needs joining at render time.

sections.meta: Counts, licence, provenance rules, and this guide.
sections.ui: Pre-assembled views: generations, timeline, milestones, highlights, facets. Start here for layout work.
sections.entities: Canonical records exactly as stored in data/*.json.
sections.graph: Flat nodes/edges with human-readable labels on every endpoint. For force-directed or matrix network views.
sections.entityDetail: Denormalized per-entity bundles: discography, crews, songs, events, relations, resolved sources. Keyed by entity id.
sections.schema: Field definitions and data rules from schema/schema.json.

renderingHints: entities.artists and ui.generations are the primary navigation: group by generation, or by city (all Yangon).
ui.timeline is pre-sorted by year; render as a vertical or horizontal chronology.
entityDetail["acid"] and entityDetail["sai-sai-kham-leng"] are the two deepest profiles and make good hero/detail pages.
graph.edges[].status and .confidence let you dim unverified links without extra lookups.
ui.facets.activeByYear is a ready-made activity series for a chart.
Sort any people-facing list by year; id slugs are for keys only, never for display.
Burmese-script aliases live in entities.artists[].aliases - keep them, do not transliterate.

ui.headline: Myanmar Hip-Hop: a sourced timeline of Yangon rap
ui.summary: From the first album in 2000 to a 2017 reunion show, this is an open, source-attributed archive of Myanmar hip-hop. Every fact links back to a citation, and every citation is marked verified, medium or low confidence.

generations.label: Precursors
generations.summary: The groundwork laid before the first records: Myo Kyawt Myaing performing from 1988, and Sai Sai Kham Leng releasing Chocolate Yaung Yayge Einmet in 2000.

generations.label: 1st generation
generations.summary: The first wave. Acid released Beginning (Sa-Tin-Gyin) in 2000, Burma's first hip-hop album, and topped the domestic charts for over two months. Theory, NS and Too Big followed.

generations.label: 2nd generation
generations.summary: The scene consolidates: 9mm, Project-1, Byauk-Oh, Examplz, G-Family, On-Track, L.E.E, Cyclone, plus the M.H.A. association and solo acts J-Me, Bigg-Y and G-Tone. Snare and the Rap Master Nay Win anchor Snare.

generations.label: 3rd generation
generations.summary: A new wave from late 2006: Jouk Jack, Kyaw Htut Swe, VIP / Rock$tar, Hlwan Paing, Ah Boy and Htein Win P Crew.

milestones.title: Myo Kyawt Myaing performing
milestones.text: The earliest figure recorded in the archive as active, treated as a pioneer of Burmese hip-hop.

milestones.title: Acid releases Burma's first hip-hop album
milestones.text: Beginning (Sa-Tin-Gyin) by Acid, founded by Phyo Zeya Thaw, Annaga, Hein Zaw and Yan Yan Chan, topped the Burmese charts for more than two months.

milestones.title: Sai Sai Kham Leng debuts
milestones.text: Debut album Chocolate Yaung Yayge Einmet, followed in 2001 by Thangegyin Myar Swar, which made him a star.

milestones.title: "One Nal Mhat Tan" hits number one
milestones.text: The track from February Mhat Tann reached number one in Myanmar.

milestones.title: Sai Sai Birthday Show begins
milestones.text: Annual outdoor concert held every 10 April from 2004, a fixture of the Yangon calendar.

milestones.title: Third generation emerges
milestones.text: From late 2006 a new wave appears: Jouk Jack, Kyaw Htut Swe, VIP / Rock$tar, Hlwan Paing.

milestones.title: Generation Wave youth movement
milestones.text: Phyo Zeya Thaw is documented as part of Generation Wave, a youth movement rather than a rap group.

milestones.title: Acid reunion at The Clubhouse
milestones.text: Straight Outta Yangon: Chapter 2, an ACID reunion show in Yangon, and the subject of Insight Myanmar episode 604.

schema.title: Myanmar Hip-Hop Open Data Archive
schema.description: Knowledge-graph style schema. All facts must carry at least one source ID and a confidence level.

fields.type: encyclopedia | article | interview | podcast | video | database | magazine
fields.title: string

fields.type: member_of | released | performed_at | pioneer_of | associated_with | mentioned_in | documented_in

rules: Every claim must reference at least one source ID.
No copyrighted text is stored - only factual metadata (names, dates, places).
Conflicts are flagged as CONFLICTED and resolved by human review, never by AI.
Burmese script names are preserved in the aliases field.
